records.issue_text: get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime value, raising TypeError and making the optimized paginator unusable (500)
records.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new path paginates audit logs with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`, so the paginator key will correspond to the `datetime` field. However `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)`. If `value` is a `datetime`, `math.floor/ceil` will raise `TypeError`, causing the optimized pagination path to 500 when enabled.
records.stripped_text: get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime value, raising TypeError and making the optimized paginator unusable (500)

records.issue_text: post_query_filter is applied after build_cursor in OptimizedCursorPaginator, so cursors are computed from unfiltered results causing rows to be silently skipped
records.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, cursors are built before applying `post_query_filter`: it calls `cursor = build_cursor(results=results, ...)` and only afterwards does `if self.post_query_filter: cursor.results = self.post_query_filter(cursor.results)`. This means `next`/`prev` cursors are computed based on the unfiltered `results`, and filtering afterwards can remove rows that were used to compute cursor boundaries, causing pagination to skip/lose items silently.
records.stripped_text: post_query_filter is applied after build_cursor in OptimizedCursorPaginator, so cursors are computed from unfiltered results causing rows to be silently skipped
